-2-  NC: 2024:KHC:14938  MFA No. 6155 of 2018  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 03.11.2017 passed in MVC No.1517/2016 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Holalkere, whereby the tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.1,16,000/- to the claimant.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Holalkere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they are referred to in the claim petition before the Tribunal.

3. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of Rs.10.00 lakhs on account of injuries suffered by the claimant in the road traffic accident that took place on 23.04.2016 at about 2.40 p.m.
when the claimant was riding his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-16/EE-4529 from Holalkere Town to his native village viz., Mallasinganahally on NH-13, near Kanive Anjaneya temple at Holalkere Taluk, the driver of Kalleshwara bus bearing registration No.KA-38-7754 drove the same in rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle of the claimant, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries on his head which is on occipital region.

Later, he was taken to NC: 2024:KHC:14938 SSIMS Hospital, Davanagere for higher treatment and incurred medical expenses of Rs.3.00 lakhs, where x-rays were taken and the Doctor noticed fracture of occipital region and he was discharged with an advice for follow up treatment.
The tribunal considering the evidence on record at Exs-P1 to P11 and considering the evidence of the claimant-PW-1, granted compensation of Rs.1,16,000/-.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that the tribunal has failed to consider the injuries sustained by the claimant and the amount that was spent towards treatment.
Injury No.2 sustained by the claimant is grievous in nature and injury No.1 is simple in nature.
The tribunal has failed to grant reasonable amount for the said injury.
He further submitted that the compensation that was granted by the tribunal was not just and reasonable one.

Further, the tribunal has not granted reasonable compensation under the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of earning during laid up period', 'conveyance attendant, food and nourishment charges' etc.,
Hence, he prayed to allow the appeal.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.1/owner of the offending vehicle and learned counsel for respondent No.2 NC: 2024:KHC:14938 Insurance company submits that the tribunal considering the medical evidence as well as oral evidence and other exhibited documents has granted reasonable D Nagaraja vs Sri H P Umesha on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161415921/
2 compensation.

entities.text: D Nagaraja vs Sri H P Umesha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They submit that no grounds are made out seeking for enhancement of compensation.

6. As there is no dispute regarding the injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident that occurred on 23.04.2016 due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA-38-7554 and liability of the insurer of the offending vehicle, the only point that arise for Court's consideration in the appeal is:-

"Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal is just and proper or does it call for interference for enhancement?
7.

After hearing the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perusing the judgment and award of the tribunal, I am of the view that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is not just and reasonable, it is on the lower side and hence, it requires to be enhanced.

C.T. Brain:-
1. Extra axial hemorrhage along left tempo parietal convexity causing compression of Ipsilateral lateral ventricle.
2. Multiple hemorrhagic contusions with perilesional edema are noticed in left frontal temporal cortex.
3. SAH is noted along left sylvian fissure, left front- temporal sulcal space.
4. Thin SDH is noted along inter hemispheric tissues and bilateral tentorium.

5. Left bone cerebral edema,
6. Displaced fracture of left zygomatic bone.
7. Oblique un-displaced fracture of right parietal bone noted extends inferiority to right occipital bone, mastoid petrous portion of one temporal bone and lateral wall of sphenoid sinus with hemosinus.

sentences.text: As per the opinion of the Doctor, injury No.2 is grievous in nature and injury No.1 is simple in nature.

The claimant was treated at Government Hospital, Holalkere initially and later he took treatment at Shamanur Shivashankrappa Institute of Medical Sciences, Davanagere as inpatient from 23.04.2016 to NC: 2024:KHC:14938 25.04.2016 and at Kasturba Hospital, Manipal from 26.04.2016 to 02.05.2016, wherein, he was treated as inpatient for a period of 10 days.

entities.text: Shamanur Shivashankrappa Institute of Medical Sciences, Davanagere
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The injuries sustained and the treatment taken by the claimant is also supported by the oral evidence of claimant and Ex-P5 wound certificate.
9. In this case, the tribunal has observed that the claimant sustained in all two injuries viz., injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2 is grievous in nature.

For one grievous injury, as per settled law, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- and for simple injury, he is entitled for Rs.10,000/- considering injury caused to temporal region and the period of treatment undergone by the claimant.
Hence, in all, he is entitled for Rs.50,000/- under the head 'pain and sufferings' as against Rs.40,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
10. The tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.28,000/- towards 'medical expenses', which is reasonable amount and no interference in that regard is called for by this Court.
11. Towards 'loss of income during laid up period', the tribunal awarded Rs.12,000/-(by considering the notional income at the rate of Rs.6,000/- p.m.).
The accident has NC: 2024:KHC:14938 occurred in the year 2016.

If notional income is taken at the rate of Rs.9,500/- p.m., as per the circular issued by the High Court Legal Services Committee, Bengaluru, the nature of injury suggest that he must have been under rest and treatment for a period of three months.

entities.text: High Court Legal Services Committee, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, a sum of Rs.28,500(Rs.9,500 x 3) is awarded under the said head as against Rs.12,000/- awarded by the tribunal by taking the notional income at the rate of Rs.9,500/- p.m.
Therefore, additional amount of Rs.16,500/- is granted under the said head.
12. The tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of amenities and unhappiness and frustration in life', which is reasonable one, hence, no interference is called for.
13. Towards 'conveyance, attendant, food and nourishment charges', etc., the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.6,000/- which is not reasonable amount.

Therefore, an additional amount of Rs.14,000/-
is awarded under this head.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation:-
 Compensation under Amount in Rs.
 different Heads

Medical expenses 28,000/-
Pain and suffering 50,000/-
Loss of amenities and 30,000/-
happiness and frustration in life Loss of income during laid up 28,500/-
D Nagaraja vs Sri H P Umesha on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161415921/
4 period Conveyance, attendant, food, 20,000/-
nourishment charges  TOTAL 1,56,500/-
Compensation awarded by the Tribunal 1,16,000/-
 BALANCE 40,500/-
15.

The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,56,500/- as against Rs.1,16,000/-
awarded by the tribunal.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER 1. The appeal is allowed-in-part.
2. The judgment and award dated 03.11.2017 passed by Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Holalkere in MVC No.1517/2016 is modified to the extent stated hereinabove.
NC: 2024:KHC:14938 3.
The claimant is entitled for an additional enhanced compensation of Rs.40,500/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of its realization.
4. Respondent No.2-The Oriental Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation together with interest within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.
5. Out of the additional compensation, the tribunal is directed to disburse the entire enhanced compensation in favour of the claimant on proper identification.

6. Draw the modified award accordingly.
7.

to transmit a copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal, along with its records.
8. No order as to costs.
